name: Norrköping
title: UTM and Ship Gauging in Norrköping | Forest, Bulk & Tankers
description: UTM and hull gauging in Norrköping for forest product carriers, container feeders, bulk ships and product tankers: holds, ballast tanks and pipework.
h1: Thickness Measurement for Cargo Ships and Tankers in the Port of Norrköping
intro: Norrköping's port lies at the inner end of Bråviken, a long inlet of the Baltic that carries ships deep into Östergötland. Its berths handle forest products, dry bulk, containers, oil products and project cargo, and the ships that carry them, from coasters and feeder container ships to small bulk carriers and product tankers, usually stay long enough for a focused thickness measurement scope. Atlantis plans each job from India and flies the technicians to the ship once the call is fixed.

highlights.h: Sheltered berths at the head of Bråviken
highlights.p: The long inlet keeps swell well away from the quays, which makes tank entry and work on deck and over the side steadier than at an open-coast port. Multi-day condition surveys on ships lying between cargoes are realistic here.

highlights.h: Product tankers at the oil harbour
highlights.p: Tankers delivering refined products to Norrköping discharge under the terminal's safety rules. Ballast tanks, deck structure, voids and deck piping can be measured during discharge when the terminal and the master agree, often as pre-docking work.

highlights.h: Forest product ships and container feeders
highlights.p: Ships loading sawn timber, paper and pulp, and feeders linking Norrköping with North Sea hubs, call on regular patterns. Hold, hatch-cover and tank-top readings fit the loading window, and recurring calls allow a larger scope to be split.

p: Ships bound for Norrköping leave the open Baltic at the mouth of Bråviken and follow a piloted fairway up the inlet, which narrows as it runs west towards the city. The port's terminals are spread along the last stretch, from berths near the city centre, where the Motala ström flows into the bay, to larger quays and storage areas further out along the inlet. It is quiet water: there is no tide to plan around, wave action is limited, and the main natural constraint is winter ice, which forms more readily in a long, narrow inlet than on the exposed coast outside. In a mild winter the fairway stays open with little help; in a cold one, icebreaker support and traffic restrictions become part of planning a call.

Norrköping is one of the larger general ports on the Swedish east coast, serving the industrial belt of Östergötland and the routes inland towards Linköping and beyond. Forest products are a core trade, with sawn timber, paper and pulp loaded for European markets, and the regional paper industry, including Holmen's Braviken mill on the north shore of the inlet, has long relied on shipping. Dry bulk moves in both directions, covering agricultural and industrial cargoes, while the container terminal links the region by feeder to the North Sea hubs. Product tankers supply fuels to the oil harbour, and project cargo and heavy units for local industry pass over the general cargo quays. The result is a port where on any given day a feeder, a timber ship and a tanker may all be working within sight of each other.

The ships that call here are mainly short-sea tonnage built for northern European trades, and many of them are ice-classed. Their gauging needs follow the cargo. Forest product carriers suffer hold and tank-top wear from forklifts and cargo handling; feeders on fixed loops need hatch covers, coamings and ballast tanks checked without missing a slot; product tankers bring the usual tanker concerns of ballast-tank coating breakdown and deck corrosion. Calls last from part of a day to a couple of days, depending on the cargo. Ships also lie at Norrköping between charters or while waiting for cargo, and those idle periods are the best opportunity for a full condition gauging that would never fit inside a loading call. Owners who know a ship will wait in Norrköping can have tanks emptied and ventilated in advance.

facilities.h: Where a ship can be gauged in the Port of Norrköping
p: Norrköping has no drydock for seagoing ships, so the work here is done afloat. At the general cargo and forest product quays, holds can be measured as cargo is worked and tank tops become accessible, and ballast tanks can be entered once the crew has emptied, ventilated and tested them. The container terminal gives shorter windows, suited to scrubber piping, hatch covers and selected ballast tanks. At the oil harbour, any work aboard follows the terminal's rules and the ship's permit-to-work system, and is usually confined to spaces outside the cargo tanks.

When a ship needs a docking it goes to a repair yard elsewhere, in Sweden or across the Baltic, and Norrköping's part in that is preparation. Gauging during a loading or discharge call shows where substantial corrosion is likely, so the yard specification and the surveyor's close-up plan can be built around measured values rather than assumptions. Ships idle at the quays between cargoes give the longest windows, with time to open and ventilate tanks one after another. Winter work at the outer berths should allow for cold, wind and short daylight, which slow external measurement far more than work inside the hull.
list: General cargo and forest product quays — hold, tank-top and hatch-coaming gauging while timber, paper or pulp is loaded.
Container terminal — scrubber wash-water lines, hatch covers and selected ballast tanks measured within the feeder's berth window.
Oil harbour — ballast tank, void and deck gauging on product tankers during discharge, with terminal approval.
Dry bulk berths — hopper, topside and cargo hold readings as the holds empty, before the next cargo goes in.
Quays used by ships between charters — full condition and pre-purchase gauging spread over several days.

context.h: Inspection regime, ice and emissions rules at Norrköping
p: Norrköping applies Paris MoU port state control through the Swedish Transport Agency, and the ships calling here are typical of the short-sea fleet that inspectors see most often: general cargo ships, small bulk carriers and feeders, many of them well into their second decade. Defects that lead to detentions on this kind of tonnage often involve hatch covers, air pipes, watertight doors and corroded deck fittings, all of which a targeted gauging scope can check before the inspector does. The EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime apply to ships of 5,000 GT and above, which brings the larger feeders and tankers into scope while leaving many of the smaller coasters outside it.

Winter shapes the year at the head of Bråviken. In cold seasons the inlet ices over, the Swedish Maritime Administration provides icebreaker assistance and may impose traffic restrictions that set a minimum ice class for ships heading in, and owners keep Finnish-Swedish ice class on their coasters partly for exactly this kind of port. Ice abrasion at the waterline, scraped coatings along the bow and the occasional indent are the marks a winter leaves, and spring is the season when owners of ice-classed short-sea ships most often ask for ice-belt readings and crack checks, so that repairs can be planned for the summer docking.

jobs.h: Gauging jobs that come through Norrköping
jobs.p: Most Norrköping jobs are commissioned by superintendents who cannot be in Sweden themselves and need a reliable set of readings from a ship that is here for cargo, not repairs. The scope is agreed against the cargo plan: which holds will be empty first, which ballast tanks the crew can prepare, and how long the terminal will keep the ship alongside. For ships lying idle between charters, the job can grow into a full condition survey, and for ice-classed coasters the spring calls are when the ice-belt work is usually added. Results are reported before the ship sails, so the superintendent can decide on the next step while the vessel is still alongside.
list: Hold and tank-top gauging on a forest product carrier during loading, with damage from cargo handling recorded by frame.
Hatch cover, coaming and scrubber piping readings on a container feeder within its scheduled berth window.
Ballast tank and deck gauging on a product tanker discharging at the oil harbour, ahead of a renewal survey elsewhere.
Spring ice-belt thickness measurement and MPI at bow frame connections on an ice-classed coaster.
Owner's condition gauging on a general cargo ship lying between charters, covering holds, double bottom and hatch covers.

logistics: Stockholm Arlanda is the usual international arrival, and trains run from Stockholm to Norrköping along the main line south; Norrköping and nearby Linköping also have smaller airports with limited connections. Sweden belongs to the Schengen area, so technicians travel from India on Schengen visas, applied for once the call is confirmed or expected with reasonable certainty. Terminal access, including the ISPS-controlled container and oil berths, is arranged by the ship's agent, who submits the team's names to the terminal operators before arrival.

faqs.q: Can a product tanker be gauged at the Norrköping oil harbour?
faqs.a: Yes, within the terminal's rules and the ship's permit system. During discharge the team can usually work in ballast tanks, void spaces and on deck structure away from hazardous zones, provided the spaces are gas-free and entry permits are issued. Cargo tank internals are left for the dry dock or a gas-free period. Everything is agreed with the terminal through the agent before the tanker berths.

faqs.q: How does winter ice in Bråviken affect a gauging job?
faqs.a: Mainly through the ship's schedule. Ice can delay arrival or shorten a stay, so we confirm the berth date with the agent before mobilising. Inside the hull, cold makes little difference to the measurements, but external readings on the shell and open decks are slower in frost and short daylight, so we put the external work into milder periods where the owner's plans allow.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock in Norrköping?
faqs.a: Not for seagoing cargo ships, so gauging in Norrköping is done afloat at the quays. That suits pre-docking estimates, condition surveys and targeted scopes during cargo work. The full renewal survey programme is usually completed at the yard the owner chooses for the docking, and the readings taken in Norrköping are referenced to the same TM plan so that both sets fit together.

faqs.q: Can cargo holds be measured while forest products are being loaded?
faqs.a: Holds that are still empty can be gauged before loading reaches them, and the cargo plan usually leaves time to do that one hold at a time. Once timber or pulp is stowed, the tank top and lower frames are covered, so the order matters. We agree the sequence with the chief officer and the stevedores so that the team stays ahead of the loading.
